children: The fiscal proposals of France's far-right National Rally party look difficult to deliver, Charlotte de Montpellier at ING says in a note. Led by Marine Le Pen, the party is well ahead in first-round election polls. It has promised 136 billion euros in annual savings, which hopes to bring public spending below 50% of GDP by 2032. While some savings appear plausible, the largest cuts are the least fleshed out, de Montpellier says. Meanwhile the party's macroeconomic assumptions--such as GDP growth of 0.9% in 2026 and 2027, followed by 1.8% in 2028--look unrealistic, she adds. "This matters all the more because the RN's plan combines fiscal consolidation with 69.3 billion euros of tax cuts and new spending in 2027 alone." (don.forbes@wsj.com)
